newsitem.title: UK: UK's grocer Sainsbury to move into banking.
newsitem.headline: UK's grocer Sainsbury to move into banking.

text.p: J Sainsbury Plc, one of Britain's biggest supermarket retailers, said on Friday that it planned to set up a banking division with the Bank of Scotland group and has applied for regulatory approval.

The bank will be 55 percent owned by Sainsbury, with the remaining stake held by Bank of Scotland. The supermarket said in a statement it had applied to the Bank of England for the green light to go ahead. If it gets clearance it will be the first supermarket to enter consumer banking.

The new bank -- to be called Sainsbury's Bank -- will be offered to 12 million customers and will kick off with two credit cards, Classic and Gold Visa, as well as additional account and card-based services, the statement said.
Sainsbury said when it launched its Reward loyalty card in June it wanted to move into financial services but industry sources had said it was unlikely before the end of this year.

Arch-rival Tesco added ClubCard Plus, a debit card with interest-paying current account, to its loyalty ClubCard just before Reward was launched and is thought to be considering other financial services as well.

Sainsbury's move, which was reported to be imminent by newspapers on Friday, seemed to help its shares up 11 pence to 361 pence while Tesco, long seen as the innovator in the sector, eased off a high of 326 pence to be 2.5 pence higher at 324.
